texts.preamble: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022 Author: Gautam Chowdhary Bench: Gautam Chowdhary High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 87 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 1532 of 2003 Revisionist :- Raj Kumar And Another Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Ashutosh Vaish,R.K.Dubey,Rajeev Chaudhary,Rajiv Chowdhury
texts.facts: It is also submitted that Criminal Revision No.1532 of 2003 was decided by the coordinate bench of this Court vide order dated 11.11.2022 which was not on merit, therefore, he moved a Criminal Appeal No.1531 of 2023 before the Hon'ble Apex Court. Brief facts of the case are that the complainant, Food Inspector inspected the shop of revisionists where flour, pulses, spices, sugar, jaggery and biscuits were placed for sale. The complainant served notice in Form No. 6 and purchased 7.50 gms. Pulse for Rs. 8.25/kg. and divided it in three equal parts and sampled it as per provisions of law. Accused was sought to sign it for which he denied. The worker in the shop of accused Girdhar signed the complain as a witness. Thereafter, they prepared sample and sent it to laboratory for analysis to CMO concerned on 16.12.1991. As per analysis report No. 16917, 1% Dal Keshari was found adulterated with the sample which is prohibited as edible goods. After the analysis report, complainant filed the complaint forwarded through the Medical Officer under Section 2(1)(l) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which is punishable under Section 7/16 of the Act. After the written consent of Medical Officer, the complaint is filed. 5. Accused were summoned in the Court, the statement of witness, Gaya Prasad Singh was recorded under Section 244 of Cr.P.C. The Court framed charges against accused under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and read over to the accused and the accused denied from the charges and seek trial. 6. The complainant Gaya Prasad Singh was again produced to record his evidence under Section 246 of Cr.P.C. The prosecution produced PW-2 Ram Janam Yadav, Food Clerk in Municipal Board, PW-3 Ashok Kumar Srivastava, Food Clerk in the office of Varanasi. After the conclusion of prosecution witnesses, statements of accused were recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. 7. Accused stated on oath in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. that whole incident is wrong, no such incident happened, Food Inspector did not inspected his shop, no sample was collected by him, no papers were signed by him at the time of inspection he was not present at shop. Accused Dashrath also stated in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. that he was not present at shop at the relevant point of time when the sample was collected by the Food Inspector. 8. Accused were awarded the opportunity of producing defence evidence but the accused did not produce any defence witness. Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129720712/ 2 9.
texts.arguments: It has been averred in the instant revision that the trail Court has erred in believing the testimony of the witnesses. He has further argued that whole approach of the trial Court, convicting and sentencing the accused-revisionist is incorrect. The impugned judgment and order suffers from gross illegality, which has resulted in miscarriage of justice and, therefore, this Court, in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 397/401 CrPC, should set-aside the impugned judgment and order passed by the Courts below be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the accused-revisionist is liable to be acquitted from the charges levelled against him. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has submitted that the trial Court has correctly analyzed the evidence, and has come to correct conclusion that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused-revisionist. He has further submitted that the impugned judgment and order has been passed by the trial Court after analyzing the evidence in detail, which is not liable to be interfered with by this Court in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 397/401 CrPC. He has further submitted that the view taken by the Courts below is not an impossible view and, therefore, this Court should not interfere with the order of conviction, and he has prayed for dismissal of the revision. Learned A.G.A. submits that notice was duly served on accused, however, they refused to sign it. The signature of their servant is taken on the complaint. It is also stated in the complaint itself that no independent witness agreed to sign the papers. The sample was prepared according to the provisions of law and sent for analysis. As per analysis report proved by complainant 0.7% Khesari found adulterated in Dal Chana. It is also submitted that as per the provisions of section 10(7), it is a mandatory requirement of law that sample should be prepared in front of one of the independent witness but it is not the requirement of law to produce them in court also. The Peon of revisionists, Girdhar Ram has signed the document, complainant and samples, however he could not be produced as evidence. He is the servant of revisionists hence the judgement passed by the trial court suffers no irregularity and the revision is liable to be dismissed. Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129720712/ 3 15. 16. The main contention of learned counsel for the revisionists is that the learned trial court as well as first revisional court analyzed the evidence of witnesses in arbitrary manner and no public witness has been produced by prosecution, the mandatory provisions are not complied with. Section 10(7) of the Food Adulteration Act states as under:- Where the food inspector take any action under clause (a) of Sub-section 1 and Sub-section 2, Sub-section 4, Sub-section 6, he shall call one or more persons to be present at the time when such action is taken and take his or their signature. 17. Learned counsel for the revisionists submits that the independent witness has not been produced in court during trial. The provisions of Section 10(7) envisages the signature of independent witness or complaint on samples, however, it does not contemplate the evidence of that person during the trial too. 18. Hon'ble Apex Court held in Ram Lubhaya Vs. Municipal Corporation Delhi 1974 (4) SCC 491 that, it is mandatory to summon independent witness at the place of occurrence at the relevant time but there examination during trial is not necessary. Section 10(7) stipulates that food inspector shall call one or more person for witnessing the proceedings of inspection, however, if they refuse for signature or cooperate with the proceedings, the Food Inspector cannot compel them for evidence. 19. In the given case, the complainant tried to summon many persons for signature on the papers as witness but they refused to participate in the proceedings, however, Peon of revisionists himself signed the papers, therefore, it cannot be termed as illegal proceedings because prosecution has undertaken the provisions of Food Adulteration Rules. 20. The second contention of learned counsel for the revisionists is that sample do not contain any material, injurious to the health of any person. No chemical adulteration is found. 24. During the course of argument learned counsel for the revisionists submitted that in case the court upheld the conviction of revisionists, the punishment may be reduced. It is submitted that this case is 23 years old, both the revisionists are old age, they are not previously convict nor they have committed any crime after this incident, the court has not given them the benefit of First Offenders Act, he had been detained in jail for 7 days he is ready to deposit the fine whichever is decided by this Court, hence it is prayed to commute the sentence. 25.
